benefit.fit: 70.1 GiB resident weights plus a memory-mapped n-gram table. Sized from headers only: GREEN on a 128 GB Mac at the full 262,144-token context (86.1 GiB needed with a 16 GiB KV reserve, against an 88 GiB shared-host ceiling). RED on a 96 GB Mac at any context — the weights alone exceed that machine's 64 GiB ceiling.
benefit.speedXStatus: measured on Apple M3 Ultra at engine build fa76a4b5: median 65.4 vs 54.9 tok/s against the 8-bit reference pack, speculative decoding disabled on every arm, 262,144-token context, concurrency 1, temperature 0, 3 prompts x 256 tokens, one warmup pass discarded, median of 3 passes; the reference arm ran first and last and drifted 0.29%. This is a ratio against the 8-bit reference, not against the full-precision model, and it holds for this host, build and prompt set only.

provenance.method: forced greedy trajectory from an 8-bit conversion (8-bit experts, projections and n-gram table) of the official BF16 weights, made with the serving engine's own converter; candidate top-1 compared by token text, resynced at each disagreement; top-20 logprobs; one server at a time with identical binary and flags; the reference trajectory was saved and replayed
provenance.confound: the 8-bit reference is not the full-precision model (token embeddings stay 4-bit in it); it shares a converter with both candidates, so a defect common to all arms would not show; TV/KL are lower bounds, weakened at 62.4% of positions here, so a small value is a floor, not closeness. Controls: self-replay 0/2560, a perturbation control 1/2560 at the perturbed position, and a paired-vs-sequential bridge that reproduced 150/2432 exactly.

boundary.scope: an 8-bit-reference comparison for one pack of one model at short context on one hardware class; the fastmlx serve launcher refuses this pack unless opted in when the model's pinned revision matches hfPin; the in-tree Swift server matches cards by repo only and does not consult it
unmeasured: other revisions of the repository (the weights at main 7eaef0fa are byte-identical but the card is pinned to ef5b919d)
